title: Socratic checklist — data extraction & lineage (提取与谱系)
rationale: Before extraction at scale, the agent audits the form, the lineage model, and the error controls. Answers are recorded; the gate checks completeness. Sources are chapter/item-level references, not page numbers.

items.question: Was the extraction form piloted on a sample of included reports, and were ambiguous fields revised before full extraction?
items.rationale: Unpiloted forms produce inconsistent fields that cannot be repaired after scale extraction.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.5 (collecting data); MECIR
items.answer_format: pilot sample size + field-level revisions + inter-extractor check on the pilot

items.question: Is each extracted value stored at its correct lineage level (report -> study -> arm -> result), with the report-study merge recorded?
items.rationale: Confusing the report with the study is the classic unit-of-analysis error (double counting).
items.source: PRISMA 2020 items 3 and 5 (report/study distinction); Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.10 (unit-of-analysis issues)
items.answer_format: lineage map + merge log for companion reports

items.question: Are continuous-outcome changes (change-from-baseline vs final values) converted to a common metric with the correlation assumptions recorded?
items.rationale: Mixing change and final values across studies biases pooled estimates; assumptions must be explicit.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.6 (combining groups / change-from-baseline)
items.answer_format: conversion rules + per-study correlation values or imputation method

items.question: Are multi-arm and shared-control studies handled so no control group is counted twice in any comparison?
items.rationale: Double-counting controls is the most frequent meta-analysis inflation error.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.10 (multi-arm and shared control designs)
items.answer_format: arm mapping per comparison + control-splitting method

items.question: Was extraction performed (or verified) by two independent actors, with disagreements adjudicated and the agreement rate recorded?
items.rationale: Dual extraction halves transcription error; the agreement rate calibrates the error risk for readers.
items.answer_format: actor identities + disagreement count + adjudication + agreement metric

items.question: Are missing, unclear, or derived values flagged per cell, with the derivation or imputation formula attached?
items.rationale: Silent imputation is undetectable in the published table and inflates confidence.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.5 and Ch.6 (imputing missing data)
items.answer_format: per-cell status flags + formula for every derived value

items.question: Does the form capture the fields required for risk-of-bias and GRADE domains (allocation, blinding, attrition counts, protocol availability)?
items.rationale: RoB and GRADE judgments are only as good as the fields extracted to support them.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.8 (assessing RoB); GRADE handbook (domains)

items.question: Are effect estimates and standard errors checked numerically (direction, units, SE vs SD vs CI confusion) for every result row?
items.rationale: SE/SD/CI confusion and sign errors are the most common numerical extraction mistakes.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.6 (obtaining standard errors from CIs and P values)

items.question: Can every cell in the published analysis tables be traced back to a source page, section, or machine-readable field?
items.rationale: Traceability is what makes a review auditable and is the reproducibility floor.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 item 11 (data items); MetaWingman lineage norm

items.question: Which single extracted field, if wrong in half the studies, would most change the pooled result?
items.rationale: The load-bearing field deserves a dedicated double-check pass.
items.answer_format: one field + the dedicated verification pass planned for it
